cues.text: Hi Bobby, go ahead and sit down. Tell me about your research project.
cues.speaker: Tutor

cues.text: Well I decided to research football, and keys for success on a football team.
cues.speaker: Bobby

cues.text: That sounds great. What are the guidelines for the test? Did the teacher talk to you about it in class?
cues.speaker: Tutor

cues.text: No, everything is on a handout that was passed out. It says that the first draft is due at the end of next week, and the second and third are due later on in the month.
cues.speaker: Bobby

cues.text: I don’t understand why we have to keep revising and fixing it. Is this assignment really that important?
cues.speaker: Bobby

cues.text: Well, this project is a major requirement for passing 11th grade English and will go on your permanent record.
cues.speaker: Tutor

cues.text: Oh really? Does that mean it will affect what English level I am placed in next year?
cues.speaker: Bobby

cues.text: Well, not exactly. You need a good grade to move on, but it is your overall grade and teacher recommendation that determines what level of English you are placed in next year.
cues.speaker: Tutor

cues.text: Anyway, tell me about your topic choice. Do you play football?
cues.speaker: Tutor

cues.text: Well, actually it’s because my father loves the sport. He watches it every weekend.
cues.speaker: Bobby

cues.text: Cool! It’s a good idea to report on something you’re interested in.
cues.speaker: Tutor

cues.text: I see you worked very hard calling players and the head coach to talk so let’s see what information you got.
cues.speaker: Tutor

cues.text: Well, you have to listen carefully to first call on the recording. It’s really hard to hear because the background noise is louder than the person’s voice.
cues.speaker: Bobby

cues.text: Yes, it is a bit tough to discern. I’m afraid the player’s answer is too short as well. You will have to interview him again and try to get him to give a better answer.
cues.speaker: Tutor

cues.text: Okay. I thought that might happen. I will call him again tomorrow.
cues.speaker: Bobby

cues.text: Moving on, let’s look back at this question.
cues.speaker: Tutor

cues.text: You asked, “Tell me about a time when you learned a major life lesson through playing football, and explain how that has shaped the person and player you have become now, and how you hope to pass on that lesson.”
cues.speaker: Tutor

cues.text: It is a great idea for a question, but in an oral interview it is far too complex. I would advise you to break it up into multiple parts to get a better response.
cues.speaker: Tutor

cues.text: I guess you’re right - I wouldn’t want to have to provide an answer to a question like that. I will simplify it.
cues.speaker: Bobby

cues.text: I found that when I asked players this question, it took too much time because they were struggling to answer the question completely.
cues.speaker: Bobby

cues.text: In fact, this is the question Joe Billings was answering when the tape ran out.
cues.speaker: Bobby

cues.text: He did tend to ramble on all the questions, didn’t he?
cues.speaker: Tutor

cues.text: He sure did.
cues.speaker: Bobby

cues.text: I would recommend that when you go back and interview players again that you use a more sophisticated recording device.
cues.speaker: Tutor

cues.text: This recording is spotty, which indicates that the equipment wasn’t working consistently.
cues.speaker: Tutor

cues.text: Okay. I guess it probably wasn’t the best idea to use the sound recorder on my phone. Hey, could you give me some feedback on the content of the report itself?
cues.speaker: Bobby

cues.text: Sure! Let’s start by focusing on your topic. While I like that you chose to cover football, it seems inexplicit.
cues.speaker: Tutor

cues.text: The keys for success of a player and team is quite an interesting topic, but what is your thesis? That is to say, what conclusions can you draw from your research?
cues.speaker: Tutor

cues.text: I would suggest coming up with a strong thesis statement and then shaping your report based on that.
cues.speaker: Tutor

cues.text: Is it really too vague? I put a whole lot of facts into it.
cues.speaker: Bobby

cues.text: I list the top 10 goal-scorers in football, and later on provide statistics for a few of the most famous coaches and their records as coaches.
cues.speaker: Bobby

cues.text: I think that’s great that you included these facts, but I think you focused too much on the facts and not enough on connecting these facts to make your point.
cues.speaker: Tutor

cues.text: Ah, I see. Okay. So it looks like I have quite a bit of work to do before the deadline!
cues.speaker: Bobby
